avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inducer; significantly reduces cyclosporine levels and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use concurrently. Monitor trough levels if recently discontinued.

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction and potential P-glycoprotein activation; may reduce cyclosporine bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; may compromise transplant rejection prophylaxis.

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit Extract
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases cyclosporine levels; risk of toxicity and nephrotoxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid completely; counsel patient on grapefruit-containing products.

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (High-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction; may decrease cyclosporine concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Limit high-dose supplements; monitor cyclosporine trough levels if used regularly.

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium Supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cyclosporine impairs renal potassium excretion; hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid unless prescribed; monitor serum potassium and renal function regularly.

caution_supplements.name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 inhibition; limited clinical data with cyclosporine
caution_supplements.action: May use with caution; monitor cyclosporine levels if high-dose therapy initiated.

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have renoprotective effects but no direct CYP3A4 interaction
caution_supplements.action: Generally safe; may be beneficial for renal function; ensure adequate monitoring.

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: No direct pharmacokinetic interaction; may support GI health
caution_supplements.action: Safe to use; may help manage GI side effects.

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and Grapefruit Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition dramatically increases cyclosporine bioavailability and blood levels; toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Absolute contraindication; educate patient to avoid all forms (juice, pulp, fresh fruit).

avoid_foods.name: Pomegranate Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition similar to grapefruit; increases cyclosporine exposure
avoid_foods.action: Avoid consumption; similar interaction profile to grapefruit.

avoid_foods.name: Seville Oranges / Bitter Oranges
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition; less well-studied than grapefruit but significant interaction potential
avoid_foods.action: Advise avoidance; includes marmalades and specialty beverages.

caution_foods.name: High-Fat Meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase cyclosporine absorption variability; affects microemulsion formulation bioavailability
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent meal timing; take with food as directed; note fatty meal variability in levels.

caution_foods.name: High-Potassium Foods (Bananas, Spinach, Potatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Cyclosporine reduces potassium excretion; additive hyperkalemia risk if excessive intake
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake; monitor serum potassium; counsel on portion control.

caution_foods.name: Licorice
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase sodium retention and potassium loss; compounds cyclosporine's hypertensive effects
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; monitor blood pressure and electrolytes.

monitoring_notes: Monitor cyclosporine trough levels regularly (target 100-400 ng/mL depending on indication and time post-transplant); assess renal function, blood pressure, and serum potassium at each visit. Counsel patients on strict avoidance of CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors and grapefruit products to maintain therapeutic levels and prevent rejection or toxicity.
